reference.source: Kaplan & Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry; DSM-5-TR
clinicalPearls: Defined by one or more distressing physical symptoms accompanied by excessive thoughts, feelings, or behaviours related to those symptoms
The diagnosis rests on the disproportionate and persistent nature of the response, not on whether the symptoms are medically explained
Features include disproportionate and persistent worry about the seriousness of symptoms, high health-related anxiety, and excessive time and energy devoted to symptoms or health concerns
Symptoms are typically persistent (often more than six months) even if individual complaints vary over time
Distinguish from illness anxiety disorder (preoccupation with having illness with few or no somatic symptoms) and from conversion disorder (neurological symptoms incompatible with recognised disease)

Management principles emphasise a consistent single coordinating clinician, regular scheduled visits, limiting unnecessary tests and referrals, and validating distress while gently shifting focus toward functioning
Cognitive behavioural therapy is the best-supported psychotherapy; treat comorbid depression and anxiety, where SSRIs or SNRIs may help
A genuine coexisting medical illness does not exclude the diagnosis, so maintain appropriate but restrained medical vigilance
reference.pathophysiology: Somatic symptom disorder is understood through a biopsychosocial model in which heightened attention to and amplification of bodily sensations, cognitive misinterpretation of benign symptoms as dangerous, and autonomic and stress responses interact. Predisposing factors include early adverse experiences, trauma, comorbid anxiety and depression, and learned illness behaviour, with reinforcement from repeated medical attention perpetuating the pattern.
additionalDifferentials: Major depressive disorder and anxiety disorders with somatic features
additionalInvestigations: Focused, proportionate medical evaluation guided by objective findings rather than repeated broad testing
Review of prior investigations to avoid duplication
Screening for comorbid depression and anxiety
Assessment of functional impairment and healthcare utilisation patterns
redFlags: New objective clinical signs suggesting an emergent genuine medical condition
Suicidal ideation associated with comorbid depression
Escalating analgesic or sedative use and dependence
Iatrogenic harm from repeated invasive investigations or procedures
reference.prognosis: Somatic symptom disorder is often chronic and fluctuating, but consistent, coordinated care can reduce distress, unnecessary investigations, and healthcare costs while improving function. Prognosis is worse with prolonged illness, multiple comorbidities, and ongoing reinforcement through repeated medical intervention.
pitfalls: Ordering repeated investigations and referrals that reinforce illness behaviour and risk iatrogenic harm
Dismissing symptoms as not real, which damages the therapeutic alliance
Assuming the diagnosis excludes genuine disease and missing a new medical problem
Failing to identify and treat comorbid depression and anxiety
Lack of a single coordinating clinician leading to fragmented, duplicated care
